newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares continue rising in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares continue rising in quiet trade.

text.p: Swedish shares continued to post gains in Tuesday morning trade, rising after New York ended higher overnight, but trade was calm .
The Stockholm general index was 1.29 percent higher at 3,171.11 at 1000 GMT in turnover of 1.75 billion crowns.
"There is a lot of money about and it doesn't seem that anyone is in a rush to sell," said one broker. "It rather seems that people are seeing buying opportunities after shortlived downturns."
Heavyweights telecoms group Ericsson and drugs major Astra were both up after Wall Street rises.
Ericsson was four crowns higher at 351.5 crowns and Astra gained three to 135.5.
The market was expecting a flurry of six month reports.

Handelsbanken was 2.5 higher at 250 crowns. It posted a slightly higher operating profit than expected for the first six months of 1997. Operating profit rose 26 percent to 3.78 billion crowns against expectations of 3.66 billion.
"All the improvement was found in lower credit losses," one analyst said.
Mining and rubber group Trelleborg was 0.5 higher at 128 ahead of its report.

The market was expecting a profit after financial items of 2.16 billion crowns including a capital gain of about 1.5 billion crowns from selling Boliden shares. Its profit this time last year was 657 million crowns.
Insurer Trygg-Hansa fell 1.5 to 172.5 crowns ahead of its report. The insurer was expected to post a pre-tax profit of 1.94 billion crowns.

Car safety maker Autoliv Inc was a winner, gaining 14.5 to 302 crowns. Market sources said U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs has Autoliv on its priority list of best valued shares.-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
